summary_md:
**[@SciFi](https://x.com/SciFi/status/2115578201422311605)** shares **Collective Emergent Alignment** (Wang, Li, Ramchurn, Huang, Dong).

Per the abstract, the authors ask whether interaction among LLM agents yields reasoning alignment beyond matched individual self-refinement. Their **REMAP** framework measures this via semantic coverage and interaction-specific gains; across model families and two multi-hop benchmarks they find broadly positive gains, strongest when evidence is spread across agents, tied to peer-information recovery and shaped by team composition and capability asymmetry.

referenced_urls.title: Collective Emergent Alignment: Measuring and Amplifying Interaction-Induced Reasoning Alignment in Multi-Agent LLMs

relevance: Quantifies when multi-agent interaction genuinely improves reasoning versus a single agent refining itself.

media.description: Screenshot of the paper's abstract on a beige background.
media.ocr_text: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems can exhibit emergent behaviors through interaction, yet whether a similar phenomenon exists for reasoning alignment remains largely unexplored. We study whether agent interaction produces additional reference-grounded reasoning alignment beyond matched individual self-refinement, and introduce REMAP (Reference-Entailment-Matrix for Agentic Process), a framework that quantifies this effect through Semantic Coverage and interaction-specific alignment gains. Across diverse model families and two multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, we observe broadly positive interaction gains, particularly on reasoning content that depends on integrating evidence distributed across agents.
